Package hadur117.core.physics

Class ShotDodger

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.physics.ShotDodger
public final class ShotDodger extends Object
DODGE-2: which simple aim the enemy's gun uses, read from the headings of its bullets we learn (those that hit us and those that meet ours), and, once one stands out, the danger of a surf option as whether that aim's bullet would cross us there.

Saguaro's ShotDodger: a gun that fires the same simple aim every time is beaten outright by standing anywhere its next bullet will not be. Its experts, per lag (SimpleAims): the six aims that are angles; the same six with the enemy's body turn on the tick after added (a gun that does not turn apart from its body); and a one-line linear aim with a divisor of its own in place of the bullet's speed, with and without that turn, the divisor learned from the bullets read as Saguaro does (a running mean decayed by 0.85 a bullet, kept within 4 to 30). The count runs across the rounds of one battle (a gun does not change its aim between rounds) and is cleared by reset(). The dodger is active only while one expert matched at least 3 of the bullets read and at least 0.6 of them; a learning gun matches none, so the surf stays on its views.

DODGE-5 (the planner's reading, planBest() and planActive()): Saguaro scores its experts loosely and learns from the bullets that missed us too. A bullet read scores every expert exp(-d^2 / 2 sigma^2) for its distance d from the bullet's heading, with sigma 0.18 of the wave's escape angle (Saguaro's 0.18 guess factor), so a gun our strict match just misses still stands out. A wave that passed us without a hit (and without meeting our bullet) contradicts every expert whose bullet would have crossed us (observePass(double[], double, double)): such a gun does not fire that aim. DODGE-4: a per-opponent expert shipped in the table primes the score (prime(int)), so the dodge acts from the first bullet; contradictions take it off again. The strict reading above is unchanged.

Pure: no engine types, no clock, no randomness.
